paper.title: CODESKILL: Learning Self-Evolving Skills for Coding Agents
paper.central_claim: Train a skill-management policy with downstream execution and behavior-alignment feedback to extract, evolve and maintain reusable coding skills that improve frozen coding agents across benchmarks.

provenance.notes: Configured seat/model supplied by invocation; no independently available provider receipt or session identifier; no probing.

sections_read: Full main text, references, Appendices A–E including training/reward/retrieval details and all prompts

evidence.quote: We therefore keep the same pipeline, action space, prompts, retrieval procedure, downstream policy, and decoding settings as
evidence.support_explanation: Prompted-curator comparison holds deployment interfaces fixed; training budgets remain different.

evidence.quote: We construct the skill bank through two preparatory passes over the test set before final evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit transductive bank acquisition; manager-training holdout is not untouched artifact holdout.

evidence.quote: We track the source instances of each skill, preserving their provenance through evolution and merging. During final evaluation, we exclude any skill whose provenance includes the current test instance to prevent access to knowledge derived from that instance.
evidence.support_explanation: Meaningful source exclusion, not a train-only bank or strict streaming protocol.

evidence.quote: Terminal-Bench 2 is not used during training, and serves as an out-of-distribution benchmark for testing whether the learned skill-management policy generalizes to new coding-agent tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Manager can transfer to a new benchmark, with its bank still constructed from that benchmark.

evidence.quote: we randomly sample 150 of the 500 Verified instances for evaluation and use the remaining 350 for RL training.
improves average pass rate from 29.32 to 40.35
evidence.support_explanation: Reported macro pass-rate gain; authors, not our reproduction.

evidence.quote: we run the frozen Qwen3.5-35B-A3B coding policy four times on each instance without injected skills, and use the average verifier score as the baseline score.
evidence.support_explanation: Reference-point execution reward controls task difficulty; not repeated main evaluation.

evidence.quote: The RL curriculum runs for 500 update steps in total, with 130, 120, and 250 steps for phases 1, 2, and 3, respectively.
evidence.support_explanation: Trainable curator and staged action curriculum are reconstructable.

evidence.quote: Retrieval is scoped to the same benchmark and same granularity, and skills generated from the same evaluation instance are filtered out to avoid same-instance leakage.
evidence.support_explanation: Benchmark-specific retrieval limits generic cross-domain bank transfer claims.

evidence.quote: The revision should be motivated by the observed outcome, such as a missing case, missing check, bad ordering, misleading guidance, or reusable caution.
evidence.support_explanation: Outcome-conditioned durable skill editing, not just collecting tasks.

signatures.object: Persistent task-level/event-driven markdown skills and manager policy
signatures.information: Normalized coding trajectories, outcomes, old skills and retrieved neighbors; training verifier plus GPT quality/alignment judge
signatures.operation: Teacher SFT then staged GRPO; extract/skip, evolve/skip, add/merge/drop; embed and retrieve skills into frozen coding executor
signatures.output: Trained Qwen3.5-4B manager and reusable skill bank
signatures.conditions: Bash-action tasks, benchmark-local retrieval, valid applicability/identity schemas
signatures.feedback: Baseline-relative verifiable task score multiplied by behavior alignment plus quality; some discrete actions quality-only
signatures.selection_rule: Learned manager decides action; no measured per-edit holdout accept/revert test
signatures.selection_data: RL training task pool; test-set preparatory rollouts build evaluation banks
signatures.persistence: Markdown skill entries updated in bank; merge replaces target; source lineage preserved
signatures.later_use: Other source-excluded instances retrieve bank entries during final evaluation
signatures.claimed_effect: Higher pass rate and fewer common-success reasoning steps
signatures.failure_boundary: Transductive acquisition, composite credit, no strict streaming or end-to-end cost evidence

gap.author_gap: Prompted skill curators optimize plausibility rather than downstream action utility; evolving and maintaining procedural skills is under-trained.
gap.checked_gap: Within same pipeline, small prompted curator little helps; learned manager improves benchmark averages. Novelty beyond prior learned memory/skill curators not independently verified.

claims.text: Learned manager improves frozen coding-agent success.
claims.setting: Three benchmarks/four groups; Qwen and GPT executors
claims.baseline_control: No skill, prompted same/stronger backbone, SFT, reconstructed memory
claims.selection_vs_test: Manager splits disjoint; bank acquired through two test-set passes with source filtering
claims.result_denominator: Qwen macro 29.32→40.35; +5.10 points over GPT prompted manager. GPT executor macro 21.80→31.62. SWE 150; Env Python43/Java107; Terminal table finite task set.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Useful learned curator in reported transductive source-excluded protocol, not clean unseen frozen-bank transfer.

claims.text: Lifecycle maintenance improves bank efficiency and quality.
claims.result_denominator: Skill bank 1252→676 with maintenance; macro pass 37.88→39.53→40.35. Java extraction-only 41.12 vs full 38.32.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Compact bank and average improvements, not uniformly better per environment or proven optimal pruning.

claims.text: Skills make task execution more efficient.
claims.result_denominator: Reported reasoning steps; training approximately20h SFT+210h RL on4 H100, excluding complete acquisition bill.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Conditional rollout-step savings; no demonstrated total-cost break-even.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A trained skill curator writes retained instruction artifacts that help other source-excluded tasks and another executor under a transductive benchmark-local bank protocol; not strictly online or pristine retained-bank transfer.

G.reason: Specific mismatch between textual skill quality and downstream utility; SkillRL/AutoSkill and reasoning memory acknowledged, but original neighboring material unavailable for first/uniqueness claims.

M.reason: Finite extraction/evolve/add/merge/drop interface; baseline-relative rollout reward and alignment couple manager to frozen reader. Quality-only discrete decisions and composite reward leave credit incompletely isolated.

X.reason: Action schemas, applicability, identity preservation, retrieval and lineage filtering are explicit; no empirical accept/revert gate, version rollback or long-stream obsolescence mechanism.

E.measurement.reason: Executable benchmark pass rates with separate issue/step metrics are relevant; common-solved steps denominator is disclosed. Judge rewards are not independently calibrated, and steps are not total cost.

E.causality.reason: No-skill, same-backbone prompted, SFT and lifecycle ablations isolate meaningful components. Reward-term and curriculum controls, exact memory reproduction and matched total budget are missing.

E.holdout.reason: Disjoint manager-training instances, new training-unseen benchmark and propagated source exclusion are useful. Yet two preparatory test-set passes and benchmark-local indexes preclude untouched retained-bank transfer or causal online adaptation claims.

E.statistics.reason: Full text Tables 1–2 give task sample sizes and mixed/negative cells, but no main-result intervals or independent manager-training/bank-construction seed variance. Four cached reward rollouts are not test replication.

E.cost.reason: Training hardware, SFT/RL hours and common-success steps supplied; acquisition passes, judges, maintenance, total failed-rollout tokens and amortization break-even are not fully priced or matched.
